Based on the search results, here are the key findings regarding Austin, TX's Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA) threshold and trip generation requirements:

## TIA Threshold Requirement

An applicant submitting a site plan, zoning, or rezoning application must submit a TIA if the expected number of vehicular trips generated by a project exceeds 2,000 net new daily trips.

## Types of TIA Analysis

The type of TIA required depends on the number of trips generated: Developments that generate over 5,000 trips per day will be required to complete a full TIA.

## Trip Generation Methodology

The TIA Determination Worksheet contains trip generation information and details of the proposed development including, but not limited to, project location, land use, access points, density, phases of site construction, and timeline for occupancy.

## Submission Process

An applicant or applicant's consultant shall first submit a Transportation Impact Analysis (TIA) Determination Worksheet to the Transportation Development Services (TDS) Division's TIA Determination Portal for review.

For more detailed technical guidelines, the City of Austin provides the Transportation Impact Analysis Guidelines document which contains specific requirements for trip distribution, analysis methodologies, and study area selection.

## Driveway Spacing Requirements

Minimum spacing to other driveways or intersections is dependent on the type of street (or Street Level) and whether it is a Minor or Major driveway.

For semicircular driveways specifically, semicircular driveways are acceptable with minimum spacing between driveway entrance and exit of 35 feet.

All one-way driveways separated by more than 15 feet (measured from edge to edge) must be signed for one-way operation.

## General Driveway Requirements

All driveways must be constructed within the street frontage of the subject property, as determined by extending the side property lines to the curb line. Neither the driveway nor the curb returns shall overlap adjacent property frontage without written approval from the adjacent property owner.

Priority shall be directed towards reducing the number of driveway approaches along Principal Roadways and Arterial streets to limit conflict points and enhance traffic flows along such roadways.

## Access Management Code

Austin's requirements are documented in the Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM). In the City of Austin, Texas, and Travis County ETJ, the maximum number of allowable site access points is dependent upon the length of the property street frontage. Minimum spacing to other driveways or intersections is dependent on the type of street and whether it is a Minor or Major driveway.

For more detailed specifications on spacing requirements for different street types and driveway classifications, you may want to consult the full Transportation Criteria Manual for Austin directly.

## TIA Requirement Threshold

An applicant submitting a site plan, zoning, or rezoning application must submit a TIA if the expected number of vehicular trips generated by a project exceeds 2,000 vehicle trips per day.

## TIA Determination Process

An applicant or applicant's consultant shall first submit a Transportation Impact Analysis (TIA) Determination Worksheet to the Transportation Development Services (TDS) Division's TIA Determination Portal for review. The worksheet contains trip generation information and details of the proposed development including, but not limited to, project location, land use, access points, density, phases of site construction, and timeline for occupancy.

The type of TIA required will depend on the application being submitted and the net new daily trips generated; more information on the types of TIAs available can be found in Section 10 of the Transportation Criteria Manual.

## Historical Context

It's worth noting that in 2017, there was a proposal to change the threshold. The proposed new threshold for requiring a TIA would be 1,000 vehicle trips per day, rather than the current number of 2,000. # Transportation Context

Property: 12713 Cinchring Ln, Austin, TX 78727 (Lot 12, Block M, Scofield Subdivision, Travis County)
Proposed use: Demolish existing single-family house; build duplex (2 units, ground-up new construction)

---

## 1. Adjacent Roadway -- Cinchring Lane

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Functional classification | Local residential street |
| ASMP street level | Level 1 |
| Ownership | City of Austin |
| Lanes | 2 (undivided) |
| Existing ROW (typical) | 50 ft |
| Future ROW (ASMP) | 50 ft (no expansion planned) |
| AADT | Not published; estimated < 500 vpd (local cul-de-sac / loop street) |
| Speed limit | 25 mph (residential default) |

Cinchring Lane is a low-volume local residential street interior to the Scofield Subdivision. Under the Austin Strategic Mobility Plan (ASMP), streets not named in the Street Network Table default to Level 1. Level 1 streets typically have a 50-ft ROW with two travel lanes and no center turn lane. No ROW expansion or street widening is anticipated.

## 2. Nearby Major Roads

| Street | ASMP Level | Functional Class | Lanes | Existing ROW | Future ROW | Est. AADT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Scofield Ridge Pkwy | Level 2 | Minor collector | 2-3 | 60 ft | 66-70 ft | ~3,000-5,000 |
| Parmer Ln (FM 734) | Level 5 | Principal arterial (TxDOT) | 6 (divided) | 120+ ft | 150 ft (ASMP) | ~45,000-55,000 |
| MoPac (Loop 1) | Level 5 / Freeway | Freeway (TxDOT) | 6-8 (divided + managed lanes) | Varies (200+ ft) | N/A (state facility) | ~90,000-120,000 |

Parmer Lane (FM 734) is the primary east-west arterial serving the Scofield area. TxDOT and CAMPO are conducting the Parmer Lane Corridor Study (FM 734 from MoPac to RM 1431) to identify capacity and safety improvements. MoPac (Loop 1) runs roughly 1 mile west of the site and provides regional north-south freeway access.

## 3. ROW Dedication

Under Austin's Transportation Criteria Manual (TCM) and ASMP, ROW dedication is required when the existing ROW is narrower than the ASMP future ROW standard. For Cinchring Lane (Level 1, 50-ft standard), the existing platted ROW in the Scofield Subdivision is expected to already meet the 50-ft standard. Therefore, **no additional ROW dedication is anticipated** for this project.

If any dedication delta were identified during site plan review, the city would require a dedication along the property frontage as a condition of the building permit or site plan approval. The City of Austin's Residential Review Guidelines (rev. November 2025) govern ROW review for residential projects.

## 4. Traffic Impact Analysis (TIA)

Austin requires a TIA when a proposed development generates **2,000 or more net new vehicular trips per day**. The TIA Determination Worksheet must be submitted to the Transportation Development Services (TDS) Division.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Existing use | Single-family detached (1 unit) |
| Proposed use | Duplex (2 units) |
| Net new units | +1 unit |
| ITE trip generation (Land Use 210/220) | ~9.4 trips/day per dwelling unit |
| Net new daily trips | ~9-10 trips/day |
| TIA threshold | 2,000 trips/day |

**Conclusion: No TIA is required.** The net new trip generation (~10 trips/day) is far below the 2,000-trip threshold. No TIA Determination Worksheet filing is necessary for a project of this scale.

## 5. Access Management -- Driveway Requirements

Austin's TCM Section 7 (Driveways) governs driveway design and spacing. For a duplex on a Level 1 local street:

- **Maximum driveways**: Typically 1-2, depending on lot frontage.
- **Driveway width**: Residential driveway maximum 24 ft (two-way) per TCM.
- **Spacing**: Minimum 35 ft between driveways (edge to edge) if semicircular layout used.
- **Setback from intersection**: Minimum 30 ft from the nearest cross-street curb return.
- **Construction**: Driveway must be constructed within the street frontage of the subject property; no overlap onto adjacent property frontage without written approval.

A single shared driveway serving both duplex units is the most common configuration and satisfies all spacing requirements.

## 6. Transit Access

### Bus Service (CapMetro)

| Route | Name | Nearest Stop | Approx. Distance | Headway |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 392 | Braker | Parmer Ln at McCallen Pass / Tech Ridge | ~1.0-1.5 mi | 30-60 min |
| 243 | Wells Branch | Howard Station / Tech Ridge | ~1.5-2.0 mi | 30-60 min |

The site is not directly served by a bus route on Cinchring Lane. The nearest CapMetro bus service operates along Parmer Lane and the Tech Ridge Park & Ride area, approximately 1.0-2.0 miles from the property. Service frequency is moderate (30-60 minute headways depending on time of day).

### Project Connect Light Rail

The Project Connect Orange Line (light rail) is planned to extend north along the N. Lamar / I-35 corridor. Future stations are contemplated at Parmer Lane and Tech Ridge, but these are **not part of the initial investment phase**. They are identified as future-phase extensions, currently undergoing environmental clearance. No construction timeline has been set for these stations. The nearest planned initial-phase station (North Lamar Transit Center) is approximately 5-6 miles south of the site.

### MetroRail (Red Line)

The existing CapMetro Red Line commuter rail has a station at Howard Station (Tech Ridge area), approximately 2.5 miles east of the site.

## 7. Bicycle and Pedestrian Infrastructure

### Sidewalks
Austin's Land Development Code and Residential Review Guidelines require sidewalks as part of residential development. For a duplex redevelopment on a local street:

- **Sidewalk requirement**: A minimum 5-ft sidewalk is typically required along the property frontage within the ROW.
- **Fee-in-lieu**: If physical constraints prevent sidewalk construction, a fee-in-lieu payment may be accepted per LDE Residential Review Guidelines.
- **Existing conditions**: Cinchring Lane in the Scofield Subdivision may have existing sidewalks on one or both sides from the original subdivision plat; the project must maintain or improve frontage sidewalk to current standards.

### Bicycle Facilities
No dedicated bike lanes exist on Cinchring Lane. As a low-speed, low-volume Level 1 residential street, shared-lane (bicycle-with-traffic) operation is the applicable standard. No bike lane construction is required as part of this project.

The nearest designated bicycle infrastructure is along Parmer Lane and MoPac frontage roads, per the Austin Bicycle Plan and ASMP Active Transportation component.

## 8. Scenic Roadway Overlay

The Austin scenic roadway overlay applies to specific designated corridors including Loop 360, RM 2222 (west of MoPac), Barton Springs Road, Lake Austin Boulevard, and others. **Cinchring Lane is not a designated scenic roadway.** Neither Scofield Ridge Parkway nor Parmer Lane in this segment carries a scenic roadway overlay designation.

**No scenic roadway overlay requirements apply to this project.**

## 9. Summary of Key Findings

| Item | Finding | Action Required |
|---|---|---|
| TIA | Not required (~10 net new trips/day vs. 2,000 threshold) | None |
| ROW dedication | No delta expected (existing ROW meets Level 1 standard) | Confirm at plan review |
| Driveway permit | Required for new driveway construction | Submit driveway permit application |
| Sidewalk | May be required along frontage | Construct or pay fee-in-lieu |
| Transit | Limited; nearest bus ~1 mi on Parmer Ln | Informational only |
| Scenic overlay | Not applicable | None |
| Bike lanes | Not required on Level 1 local street | None |
